body:
Global crypto markets closed Monday in the red, with total market capitalization falling to $2.85T, a -4.19% drop over 24 hours on volume of $129.5B. The session had the texture of a controlled unwind rather than a panic flush: BTC dominance held at 58.2% and ETH dominance at 11.4%, suggesting rotation out of altcoins rather than outright risk-off liquidation. The Fear & Greed index actually ticked higher, from 70 yesterday to 74 today, which tells you the crowd still leans constructive even as prices slide. That divergence between price action and sentiment is worth flagging — it has historically preceded either a sharp recovery or a sentiment reset, and right now the setup is ambiguous enough to respect both outcomes.

Bitcoin printed $82,775 on the session, off -2.14% over 24 hours and -1.96% on the week, with volume at $36.71B. The hourly is nearly flat at +0.06%, so the selling pressure appears to have stalled near current levels rather than accelerating into the close. The $82,000 area is the immediate line in the sand; a clean break below it on volume would open a test of the mid-$70,000s, which is where the next meaningful demand cluster resides based on prior consolidation structure. On the upside, bulls need a reclaim of the mid-$80,000s with conviction to re-establish the trend. Noteworthy: according to Cointelegraph, Strategy added 1,665 Bitcoin for $143M this week, pushing its total stack to 847,666 BTC — that kind of institutional bid at these levels reinforces the floor narrative and is not nothing.

Ethereum held up better than the broader market on a relative basis, sliding -1.07% over 24 hours to $2,658.98 on $14.39B in volume, making it the second-best performer among ZIMR tracked majors. The real divergence story is Chainlink, which posted +1.08% on the day and an eye-catching +12.65% on the week — the standout performer by a wide margin. The catalyst appears linked to Chainlink's update of its cross-chain bridge infrastructure, a move CoinDesk notes came months after a $292 million hack at a rival exposed systemic risks in that space; LINK buyers are pricing in a competitive moat. On the other side of the ledger, UNI collapsed -10.20%, AVAX shed -6.52%, DOT fell -6.03%, and ADA dropped -5.24% — all of this while XRP and SOL managed to stay positive on the 7-day timeframe at +2.30% and +2.59% respectively, even as they gave back ground on the day. The selective nature of the carnage, with LINK bucking the trend and the layer-1 basket showing a wide dispersion, suggests capital is already becoming more discerning ahead of whatever altseason materializes next.

The macro backdrop is providing no obvious tailwind right now. With funding rates and open interest data unavailable for today's session, positioning signals are opaque, but the volume and price action are consistent with a market digesting a recent run rather than breaking down structurally. Regulatory tone in Europe is shifting, with ESMA's chair signaling that MiCA enforcement is moving from rulemaking into active supervision — a transition that adds compliance pressure to European-facing operations in Q4. On the institutional side, Franklin Templeton's decision to bring its tokenized collateral service to Bybit is a quiet but meaningful signal that real-money firms are deepening their market structure integration regardless of near-term price noise. Apollo's Torsten Slok raising concerns about AI agents draining cheap bank deposits is the kind of systemic-risk framing that eventually finds its way into regulatory conversations and could color sentiment around DeFi and on-chain finance more broadly.

Into the week's final sessions, the key catalyst watch is whether BTC can defend $82,000 and print a positive weekly close — Cointelegraph is flagging this could be Bitcoin's best Q3 in 9 years if it holds, which adds a psychological dimension to Friday's close that traders will not ignore. A failure to hold current levels with volume pickup would shift the near-term bias decisively bearish. Watch LINK for any fade of the weekly surge; a pullback that holds above prior resistance would confirm the breakout. UNI's -10.20% single-day drop demands attention — either there is fundamental news not yet fully reported, or it becomes a value entry depending on what drives the next 24 hours. The broader risk is that greed readings near 74 combined with softening prices create the conditions for a sentiment snapback lower, particularly if macro data out of the US this week prints hot and rekindles rate concern.
